title: Serving runtime: architecture, kernel scheduling, profiling & benchmarking playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This page consolidates the production-facing documentation for the serving runtime: architecture overview, kernel selection and scheduling policy, profiling playbooks, benchmarking suite, release notes, known issues, operational runbooks, and the team wiki index. It is intended for engineers on the runtime, infra, SRE, and applied ML teams who operate or extend inference infrastructure.

Goals and scope:
- Explain the components and data/control plane flows for the runtime.
- Document deterministic kernel-selection and scheduling behavior used for production rollouts.
- Provide reproducible profiling guidance and the standard benchmarking harness.
- Maintain a single source of truth for runbooks (latency, OOMs, capacity) and recently shipped release notes.

1) Runtime architecture (high level)
Overview:
The runtime is composed of the following logical services: runtime-proxy, schedulerd, kernel-selector, batch-coordinator, kv-cache, worker-agent, profiling-agent, and telemetry-exporter. These services run on dedicated roles in k8s or on bare-metal racks for Dedicated deployments.

Data/control plane flows (short):
- Inference request enters runtime-proxy (edge), which enforces auth, quotas, and initial routing policy.
- Proxy forwards to schedulerd, which performs fast path routing to warm workers or routes to batch-coordinator for batched requests.
- Worker-agent executes kernels chosen by kernel-selector and manages the KV cache and per-request KV lifecycle.
- Kernel telemetry emitted to profiling-agent and telemetry-exporter for metrics, traces, and perf counters.

Key components and responsibilities:
- runtime-proxy: TLS termination, token validation, per-route SLO enforcement. Ownership: runtime-networking.
- schedulerd: Request routing by policy (latency/cost/region/model-capabilities). Ownership: serving-runtime.
- kernel-selector: Maps model architecture, quantization profile, and sequence-length distribution to an optimal kernel set (CUDA/cuBLAS/ROCm kernels). Ownership: runtime-optimization.
- batch-coordinator: Continuous-batching layer, responsible for formation and dispatch of micro-batches. Configurable batch windows and max-batch-size. Ownership: serving-runtime.
- kv-cache: Prefix and KV caching service (memory-backed per-node), with transparent invalidation hooks. Ownership: cache-team.
- worker-agent: Hosts the model execution runtime, memory management (attention caches), and GPU kernel execution.

SLOs and operational targets:
- Availability: 99.95% per-month for hosted runtime endpoints.
- Latency targets (per-token streaming; measured at runtime-proxy): p50 < 30ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for small/medium models on Dedicated pools.
- Throughput targets: dependent on SKU; each GPU worker must sustain at least 80% of the calibration throughput in steady-state.
- Error budget policy: incidents that burn >10% of monthly error budget trigger incident review and mitigation checklist.

2) Kernel scheduling & selection policy
Principles:
- Deterministic mapping: kernel-selector returns a deterministic kernel set given model_id, quantization_profile, device_capabilities, and target_sequence_len. This makes rollouts auditable.
- Cost-aware fallbacks: schedulerd can route to cheaper quantized kernels or smaller model variants when load or SLOs require it.
- Preference order: optimized fused kernels > vendor-tuned kernels > reference kernels.

Selection inputs (examples):
- model_signature: gpt-3-small-v2
- quant_profile: int8-q4f16
- device: a100-80gb
- sequence_target: 512 tokens

Example kernel mapping (table-like text):
| condition | selected kernel | fallback kernel | notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| model=gpt-3-small-v2, device=a100-80gb, seq<=512 | fused-attn-v2 | vendor-attn-v1 | fused-attn-v2 preferred for latency |
| quant=int8-q4f16 | q8-fused-attn | q8-ref-attn | q8 kernels reduce memory by ~3x |

Kernel configuration snippet (YAML):
kernel_config: |
  model_id: gpt-3-small-v2
  device_profile: a100-80gb
  sequence_thresholds: [256, 512, 1024]
  preferred_kernels: ["fused-attn-v2", "vendor-attn-v1"]
  fallback_kernels: ["ref-attn-v1"]

Kernel rollout and testing checklist:
1. Add kernel to canary pool (kernel-selector config update).
2. Run unit kernels' microbenchmarks (latency/throughput per sequence length).
3. Run QA on benchmark harness (see section 4) against representative prompt sets.
4. Monitor key metrics for 72 hours: p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, memory watermark, L2 cache misses.
5. If metrics regress >5% p95 latency or cause memory OOMs, revert to previous kernel and open a regression-triage ticket.

3) Profiling playbook (how to profile, tools, and artifacts)
When to profile:
- New kernel onboarding, model version updates, unexplained tail latency, or recurring OOMs.

Tools and agents:
- profiling-agent: collects per-kernel counters, GPU power/SM utilization, and process-level traces.
- perf-bench: internal CLI wrapper to run microbenchmarks and capture flamegraphs.
- nsight/rocprof integration for deep GPU traces when needed.

Standard profiling steps:
1. Reproduce with a stable prompt set (use bench-suite profile prompts) and capture baseline.
2. Run perf-bench with flags: --mode=latency --runs=500 --sequence=512 --capture=flamegraph --out=artifact.tgz
3. Upload artifact to the profiling S3 bucket: aws s3 cp artifact.tgz s3://redwood-profiles/2027-09-15/
4. Open profiling ticket with artifacts and tag runtime-profiling. Include p50/p95/p99, SM utilization, and memory watermarks.

CLI example:
- invctl profile --service worker-agent --model gpt-3-small-v2 --sequence 512 --runs 500 --out /tmp/prof.tgz

Artifacts to produce:
- JSON summary of microbenchmarks (latency, throughput), flamegraph SVG, per-kernel perf counters CSV, and Nvidia/AMD profiler report.

Acceptance criteria for a kernel change:
- p95 latency no worse than previous by >5% on representative workloads.
- No increase in OOM occurrences across 10,000 synthetic requests.
- Throughput within ±10% of baseline for the same GPU SKU.

4) Benchmarking suite (bench-suite)
Purpose:
A reproducible harness to measure latency and throughput across permutations of model, quantization profile, sequence length, and batch size. Results are stored in benchDB and used for model catalog performance profiles.

Components:
- bench-orchestrator: launches controlled experiments against worker pools.
- bench-driver: client that generates synthetic request streams according to a workload spec.
- benchDB: Postgres-backed store containing run metadata and aggregated results.
- reference prompt sets: stored under s3://redwood-bench/prompts/*.jsonl

Standard experiment config (example JSON described in text):
- model: gpt-3-small-v2
- quant_profile: int8-q4f16
- device: a100-80gb
- sequence_lengths: [64, 256, 512, 1024]
- concurrency: [1, 4, 16]
- runs_per_point: 200

Running a benchmark (example):
1. Prepare environment: ensure bench-orchestrator has access to dedicated canary pool.
2. Start bench-driver: benchctl run --config canary-exp-2027-09-15.json --out results/
3. Upload to benchDB: benchctl ingest --dir results/ --db-url $BENCH_DB
4. Review dashboard: /dashboards/bench-suite/latest

Bench metrics collected:
- per-token latency (p50/p95/p99), total response latency, GPU utilization, memory watermark, kernel execution time breakdown, batch formation time.

Interpretation guidance:
- If per-token p95 increases with concurrency but GPU util remains low, inspect batch formation and kernel queuing (batch-coordinator metrics).
- If GPU util is saturated and p99 spikes, consider autoscaling or routing to larger SKUs.

5) Release notes (recent highlights)
- 2027-09-10 v2027.09.0: Kernel: fused-attn-v2 promoted to stable for a100-80gb; default kernel-selector rule updated. Reduced p95 by ~12% on small models.
- 2027-07-22 v2027.07.1: Fix for KV cache invalidation bug that caused stale prefix responses in rare multi-tenant cases. Patch rolled to all dedicated pools.
- 2027-05-03 v2027.05.0: Introduced profiling-agent v2.0 with reduced overhead and additional SM-level counters.

Upgrade and rollback policy:
1. Deploy kernel-selector config only to canary pool (10% of traffic).
2. Run bench-suite experiments for 24h and monitor regressions.
3. Promote to 50% if metrics within acceptance.
4. Full rollout after 72h stable monitoring.
5. Rollback: update kernel-selector to previous fingerprint and drain canary workers gracefully using schedulerd drain API.

6) Known issues (active and triaged)
- Issue: occasional P99 spike when KV cache eviction coincides with large-batch formation.
  - Status: triaged. Owner: cache-team. Mitigation: increase cache watermark by 20% on affected pools; short-term fallback to smaller batch windows.
- Issue: rare OOM on a100-40gb with seq>2048 using int8-q4f16 kernels.
  - Status: investigating. Owner: runtime-optimization. Mitigation: temporarily route seq>2048 to vendor-attn-v1.
- Issue: profiling-agent v1 reports inflated SM util on ROCm machines (false positive).
  - Status: fixed in profiling-agent v2; upgrade required.

How to report new issues:
1. Create an issue in the runtime JIRA project with labels: runtime, severity, kernel.
2. Attach bench-suite or profiling artifacts and link to benchDB run id.
3. Assign owner via oncall rotation or routing rules.

7) Runtime runbooks (operational procedures)
Runbook: High tail latency (p99 spike)
1. Triage: Check /dashboards/runtime-latency for affected models and pools.
2. Identify scope: is it single-region, single-pool, or global?
3. Run benchctl quick-run for an affected model and sequence length: benchctl quick --model $MODEL --seq $SEQ --concurrency 4 --head 100
4. If kernel regressions suspected, pin kernel-selector to previous fingerprint: kubectl apply -f kernel-selector-pin.yaml
5. If memory pressure, increase KV cache watermark or reduce max-batch-size on the batch-coordinator.
6. Notify customers per escalation policy if SLAs are impacted.

Runbook: GPU OOMs on workers
1. Identify worker pod and tail logs: kubectl -n runtime logs pod/$POD --previous
2. Check worker-agent memory watermark and recent kernel changes.
3. If kernel change is implicated, revert kernel-selector mapping for that model_id.
4. If persistent, cordon the node and repro with reduced batch sizes; collect nsight/rocprof traces and open a regression ticket.

Runbook: Canary kernel regression
1. Immediately reduce canary traffic to 0% using schedulerd control plane: schedulerctl set-canary traffic 0
2. Roll back kernel-selector config to previous stable fingerprint.
3. Invalidate KV cache if necessary to avoid stale states: cachectl invalidate --scope canary
4. Postmortem and SLA impact assessment.

Onboarding checklist for new engineers:
1. Read the architecture overview and kernel-selector design doc.
2. Run benchctl quick runs against the canary pool and review benchDB results.
3. Shadow the oncall for two rotations.
4. Complete the kernel onboarding labs (lab instructions: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-onboarding-labs).

Appendix: Examples and commands
- Pin kernel-selector example:
  kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
  apiVersion: v1
  kind: ConfigMap
  metadata:
    name: kernel-selector-config
  data:
    fingerprint: "f3a9d2b4-2027-09-10"
  EOF

- profiling CLI example:
  invctl profile --service worker-agent --model gpt-3-small-v2 --sequence 512 --runs 500 --out /tmp/prof.tgz

- benchctl quick-run example:
  benchctl quick --model gpt-3-small-v2 --sequence 256 --concurrency 4 --runs 200
